# 01 System Architecture Overview

Shiftly is a modern, event-driven enterprise workforce marketplace built using a monorepo architecture (Turborepo + pnpm). The system leverages a scalable microservices backend powered by NestJS, communicating asynchronously via Kafka, and serves users through a responsive React (Vite) frontend.

This diagram illustrates the primary actors and the boundaries of the Shiftly system.

![Mermaid Diagram](https://mermaid.)

## Microservices Container Architecture

The backend is composed of discrete, domain-driven microservices. All external client traffic is routed through the API Gateway, while internal service-to-service communication relies heavily on Kafka for asynchronous event streaming.

![Mermaid Diagram](https://mermaid.)

## Core Architectural Principles

1. **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**: Each microservice owns its domain. Database tables are isolated into separate PostgreSQL schemas (e.g., `identity`, `jobs`, `applications`) preventing cross-domain joins.
2. **Event-Driven Architecture**: To avoid synchronous blocking calls between services, Kafka is used extensively. For example, when a user registers in `identity-service`, an event is emitted to Kafka which `user-service` and `notifications-service` pick up asynchronously.
3. **Transactional Outbox Pattern**: Used to ensure data consistency between local PostgreSQL transactions and Kafka event publishing.
